A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 4D-VLA research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching across section moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LIBERO and MV-Bench simulations, real-world robot experiments, component ablations and controlled coordinate-chaos experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds RLBench results and a comparison of frame-sampling methods with success, latency and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The spatial embeddings, temporal token construction, memory-bank sampling algorithm, MLP action head and losses remain unchanged. The added appendix experiments specify benchmark-specific input configurations and alternative samplers without revising the proposed 4D-VLA algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds a focused four-task RLBench evaluation covering grill removal, button pressing, wine placement and drawer opening (Appendix 7.1). This extends simulated manipulation coverage within the existing domain. The multi-view real-world tasks are retained from v1's appendix, not newly introduced.

E2.justification: The comparison set expands substantially: Table 6 introduces C2FARM-BC, LLARVA, PerAct and ARM4R, while Table 8 compares MBS with Adaptive Pooling, Grid Pooling and a per-frame Q-Former. These add comparisons against 3D pretraining and video-style sampling approaches. Existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New experimental settings include the ARM4R protocol with current front and wrist views, front-only history and random-crop augmentation. The added sampler comparison uses InternVL2.5-4B on LIBERO-Spatial for 20 epochs and measures latency and peak memory alongside success. Previously reported protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix 7.2 adds a focused analysis of sampling alternatives, testing MBS against video-style compression methods and single-frame input on accuracy and resource cost. Existing window-size, temporal-encoding, action-head, input-component and coordinate-chaos analyses are retained, including those moved between sections.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three evaluation seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting for the original LIBERO comparison. Existing uncertainty displays are retained. The added tables report point estimates without introducing new run-count disclosures, uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Two substantive result sets are added. Table 6 reports RLBench averages of 77.4 for 4D-VLA and 71.9 for ARM4R. Table 8 reports MBS success of 0.866, latency of 160.0 ms and peak memory of 8682.9 MB. These are newly reported experiments; matched original results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The spatial back-projection, temporal-token formulation, losses and coordinate-transformation equations remain unchanged, including Equation 5 in the relocated chaos analysis. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about mitigating coordinate/state chaos, using memory-bank sampling and improving spatial generalization with MV-Bench. The new experiments support these existing contributions rather than redefine their scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies the ARM4R comparison by acknowledging calibrated intrinsics/extrinsics as additional supervision. It also adds explanations involving sampler sensitivity, spatial-information loss and compatibility with streaming control. The original RGB-D hardware limitation and proprioceptive-overfitting interpretation remain.

D1.justification: The additions document view selection, cropping, pooling thresholds of 0.99/0.96, grid compression and query counts for reproducing the new comparisons. The project link changes from fudan-zvg to LogosRoboticsGroup. Original pretraining, fine-tuning and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to history-concatenating policies, ARM4R, the new RLBench comparators, LongVU and LLaMA-VID. Appendix 7.1 explicitly distinguishes action-centric, calibrated image-patch pretraining from ARM4R's point-cloud/proprioceptive representation learning. These are focused positioning additions; the broader related-work narrative remains.

P1.justification: The multi-view real-world evaluation moves from Appendix 7.2 to Section 4.6, while the head/component ablations move from Section 5.2 to Appendix 7.2. Local prose, terminology and front-matter edits accompany an acknowledgment addition. Most existing text is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the RLBench and sampler-comparison tables. Existing multi-view displays and the component-ablation table are relocated and renumbered, with some caption revisions and page reflow. The original diagrams, plots and their visual content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the ARM4R comparison and sampler accuracy/resource analysis provide more relevant scrutiny of the proposed components, while calibration qualifications and implementation details improve transparency. The gains are limited: new results lack uncertainty estimates, and Appendix 7.2 overstates the speed advantage because Table 8 shows Adaptive Pooling at 150.7 ms versus MBS at 160.0 ms.
